title: ZFS
description: ZFS pools, disks and datasets -- principally file01, which holds the media archive. Pool, scrub, error and dataset numbers come from the textfile collector installed by roles/node_exporter; ARC and pool I/O come from node_exporter's built-in zfs collector. Provisioned by roles/node_exporter_scrape; edits made in the UI are overwritten on the next Ansible run.

panels.title: Pools
panels.description: The whole pool-level picture in one row each. "Last scrub" is the age of the last completed scrub; a pool that has never finished one reads as the age of the epoch, which is deliberate -- never scrubbed and scrubbed far too long ago are the same problem.

panels.title: Devices
panels.description: Every vdev and leaf disk in the selected pools, with the cumulative error counters zpool status reports. Checksum errors are the interesting column: they are silent corruption that ZFS caught and repaired, and a disk that starts producing them is on its way out long before the pool leaves ONLINE. The counters reset on "zpool clear".

panels.title: New device errors
panels.description: The same counters, differenced. Flat zero is the expected shape -- any step at all is worth chasing, which is why ZfsDeviceErrors alerts on more than zero rather than on a rate.

panels.title: Pool capacity used
panels.description: Dashed lines are where ZfsPoolCapacityHigh and ZfsPoolCapacityCritical fire. A copy-on-write pool fragments and slows down well before it is actually full; 80% is the conventional place to start worrying.

panels.title: Pool free space
panels.description: The absolute number behind the percentage next door -- the one that tells you how many more days of recordings fit.

panels.title: Free-space fragmentation
panels.description: How broken up the pool's free space is, not how broken up its files are. Rises as a pool fills and stays there -- the only real cure is more free space.

panels.title: Dataset space used
panels.description: Per-dataset, including descendants. On file01 this is where archive/media growing and archive/media-staging being reset each Monday show up (see roles/media_staging_reset).

panels.title: Datasets
panels.description: Compression is logical bytes divided by physical -- 1.00 means the dataset is not compressing, which for video is the expected answer. Quota reads 0 where none is set.

panels.title: ARC size
panels.description: ZFS's read cache, and the ceiling it is allowed to grow to. Unlike the page cache this is counted as used memory, so a large ARC on file01 is normal and not a leak. From node_exporter's own zfs collector, not the textfile script.

panels.title: ARC hit rate
panels.description: Reads served from RAM. A media archive streamed once and never re-read has no business having a high hit rate; this matters when it drops for a workload that used to be cached.

panels.title: Pool read/write throughput
panels.description: From the per-pool io kstat. Some OpenZFS versions no longer publish that kstat, in which case this panel stays empty and the disk throughput panel on the Hosts dashboard is the thing to read instead.

panels.title: Collector run time
panels.description: How long zfs-textfile-collector takes, and how old its output is. The age line climbing instead of sawtoothing means the timer has stopped and every panel above is frozen -- ZfsMetricsStale alerts on exactly that.
